Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
344 PM EDT Wed Jul 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
We continue to monitor the development of showers and
thunderstorms this afternoon from Central Virginia to Southern 
Maryland.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A few strong to severe thunderstorms are possible from
  Central Virginia to Southern Maryland this afternoon. 
  
- 2) Below average temperatures and mainly dry conditions are
  expected Thursday through Saturday.

- 3) Gradual increase in moisture & precipitation chances early
  next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A few strong to severe thunderstorms are
possible from Central Virginia to Southern Maryland this 
afternoon.

Surface observations and visible satellite show surface 
convergence becoming maximized from Central Virginia to 
Southern Maryland as a cold front overtakes a pre-frontal trough
that was already in place. Thus far, showers have struggled to 
mature, with very few, if any, producing lightning. This is 
likely due to ample dry air present in the mid-upper levels 
evident on both the 12z IAD sounding and model soundings. As
low-level convergence continues to increase from Central
Virginia to Southern Maryland, it may eventually be enough to
overcome the dry air and sustain the development of thunderstorms.
If a more robust storm were to develop, there could be a
conditional threat for it to become severe, with damaging winds
being the primary threat. Parameter-wise the environment is
impressive, with around 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE, 50-60 knots of
effective bulk shear, and DCAPE over 1000 J/kg. However, this
could be a case where the high DCAPE, highly sheared environment
is also proving unfavorable for maintaining deeper updrafts. So
there's a conditional severe thunderstorm threat late this
afternoon into this evening, with damaging winds being the
primary threat. SPC has far southern Maryland outlooked in a
Slight (level 2 of 5) Risk for severe thunderstorms, with a
Marginal (level 1 of 5) Risk extending a bit further north and
west. Any showers or storms should gradually wind down through
the evening, with drier conditions expected during the second
half of the night. Cooler, drier air will start to filter in
behind the front, with overnight lows dropping back into the 50s
to the west of the Blue Ridge, with low-mid 60s further east.
 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Below average temperatures and mainly dry
conditions are expected Thursday through Saturday.

A sprawling area of high pressure will build to our north for 
Thursday and Friday, before shifting off the New England 
Coastline on Saturday. Northerly flow ahead of the approaching 
high will advect a much cooler and drier airmass into the region
for Thursday. Well below normal temperatures and dewpoints are 
forecast for late July, with high temperatures only in the upper
70s/low 80s. Dewpoints in the 50s will also make it feel much 
less humid than is typical for July. Mostly sunny skies will 
accompany the well below normal temperatures/dewpoints. 
Temperatures will stay well below normal for Friday and Saturday
within easterly flow. Some moisture could be drawn northward
from the stalled frontal zone across the southeastern states
during this time. The current forecast has some low rain chances
both days, mainly in southern portions of the CWA and along the
Allegheny Mountains.

KEY MESSAGE 3... Gradual increase in moisture & precipitation 
chances early next week. 

Broad high pressure will continue to shift northeast over the 
weekend, with low pressure building over northeastern Canada 
and a stemming trough potentially forming over the Mid-Atlantic late 
Sunday and into Monday. Dewpoints start to increase during this 
time, so shower & thunderstorm chances could increase during the 
afternoon & evening hours Sunday and Monday as this perturbation 
moves through. Machine-learning algorithms show some lower-end 
probabilities for severe occurrence during this time, although 
ensembles still show uncertainty in timing of the overall synoptic 
setup. As this trough approaches, temperatures gradually begin to 
increase back into the upper 80s.

Dewpoints could remain elevated within the region as this system 
moves through, with the upper-level low to the north slowly 
tracking to the south before shifting to the northeast midweek. This 
could overall re-introduce chances for rain within the region 
after a brief dry spell. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected at the terminals today. 
We continue to monitor the development of showers and 
thunderstorms especially to the south of DCA. PROB30s have been 
maintained in the TAF for both DCA and CHO, but coverage of 
storms appears to be lesser than has been advertised by most 
guidance thus far. Any threat for showers and storms should 
gradually wind down this evening. Thereafter, predominantly VFR
conditions are expected at the terminals through Saturday. Lower
ceilings could briefly be possible in easterly flow on Friday or
Saturday. Winds will predominantly be out of the west to
northwest today, north later tonight into tomorrow, and then
east to southeast on Friday and Saturday.

Predominantly VFR conditions are anticipated across terminals Sunday 
and Monday, although a few scattered showers and thunderstorms in 
the afternoon/evening hours could temporarily cause reduced 
conditions during this period. Light southeasterly winds briefly 
shift southwesterly by Monday evening. 

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory conditions are ongoing at most locations 
this afternoon within westerly flow. SMWs may also potentially 
be needed this afternoon as showers and thunderstorms move over 
the waters. Winds shift to out of the north tonight, with SCAs 
in effect within channeled northerly flow for the main stem of 
the Bay and the Lower Tidal Potomac. Northerly winds gradually 
decrease through the day tomorrow, before turning out of the 
east to southeast for Friday and Saturday.

Winds remain below SCA thresholds through Sunday and Monday, with 
southeast winds shifting southwesterly by Monday evening. Scattered 
showers & thunderstorms could bring some gustier winds over the 
waters in the afternoon & evening hours during this period. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Water levels are expected to decrease within north to
northwesterly flow behind a cold front. Anomalies gradually
rebound within easterly flow this weekend, with more sensitive 
locations potentially reaching Action Stage.

&&
